tactic_quiz.setup: You pull up the screenshot. A red banner fills the browser window: [i]"THREAT DETECTED - 3 infected files found. Do not restart your device. Call support immediately."[/i]
tactic_quiz.question: What is the one fact that proves this pop-up was fake, before anybody even called the number?

milestone.title: Tactic Identified: The Impossible Scan
milestone.detail: Recognized that a web page in a browser cannot scan a device's files - so any pop-up claiming to have found infections is fabricated by definition.

options.text: A web page in a browser cannot scan the files on your computer.
options.feedback: A website cannot see the files on your computer. It cannot count your infected files because it cannot see them. Any page that claims a specific number of threats made that number up - which makes every one of these pop-ups fake, no exceptions.

options.text: Real antivirus software never uses red warning banners.
options.feedback: Plenty of real security tools use alarming colors. Judging by looks is exactly the trap - these pages are designed to look right. What gives it away is that a browser page cannot scan the machine at all.

options.text: The message had a phone number instead of a support link.
options.feedback: A phone number is a strong warning sign - real security software fixes things in the software, it does not ask you to call a stranger. But the airtight proof is simpler: the page could never have detected anything in the first place.

options.text: It told him not to restart his device.
options.feedback: That line is there to stop him closing the page and clearing his head, so you are reading the intent right. Still, the fact that settles it is that a web page cannot look at his files to begin with.
